newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia plans to make global bond issue - Kasyanov.
newsitem.headline: Russia plans to make global bond issue - Kasyanov.

text.p: Russia is likely to make a global bond issue this autumn and plans to issue three Eurobonds, including probably at least one in yen, in 1998, a senior Finance Ministry official said.

"In the very near future we shall start working on getting permission for making a global issue," Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov told Reuters in a weekend interview, referring to the international regulatory approval required to launch the issue.
He added adding that the issue would most likely be denominated in dollars.
"We are not ruling out the possibility of issuing very long-term, 20- or 30-year, paper in the autumn," Kasyanov said.

Russia issued its first $1 billion five-year Eurobond last November. It was followed by a two billion mark Eurobond in March. Russia will hold roadshows for its next dollar Eurobond from June 11 to 18.
A global issue gives freer access to Russian debt for many investors -- for instance pension funds -- to buy the paper directly, bankers say.
Last week a senior Finance Ministry official said Russia planned to raise $3 billion through Eurobond issues in 1998.
"There will most likely be three Eurobond issues next year," Kasyanov said in the interview. "We have not yet taken a final decision, but one issue is likely to be done in yen."
The 1997 budget provides for total foreign borrowing at $3.4 billion dollars of which Russia has already issued $1.2 billion.
"We are not ruling out that...there may be a decision on increasing the volume of the issues," Kasyanov said.
